The last date to receive applicable service and support for the DPoP r99 and earlier releases. The product becomes obsolete. if you have any questions.
EOL for the Secure Forwarder Steering Function
Netskope announces the end-of-life and support for the Secure Forwarder steering function. The Secure Forwarder steering function will not be available on physical and virtual appliances effective October 31, 2023.
Netskope recommends that you migrate to other steering mechanisms that are suitable for your use case as outlined in Netskope’s Traffic Steering documentation. Please contact your Customer Success Manager to discuss your migration plans or for any guidance. We value your feedback and are happy to learn about your migration plan and provide assistance.
For the most current information, refer to:
End of Support for Secure Forwarder Steering Function
on our Support site.

It gives 12 months for customers to move to a supported release. For example, appliance release 77 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 99 goes live. Releases that are outside the Netskope support period:
Are not guaranteed to work with the latest cloud releases.
Are no longer tested by Netskope.
Do not receive hotfixes.
Do not receive new feature updates.
At our discretion, we may provide support for releases outside our support period. If a customer encounters an error in a version of software that is other than the latest release, Netskope may require the customer to upgrade to a specified later version to obtain a correction of the error.

Upgrading to version 93.1.0
Before downloading the upgrade package, ensure the following:
You are running a minimum version 71.x. Upgrade is supported on two versions ahead of the current version. If you are running appliance versions older than 71.x or if the root (/) partition is less than 64 GB, you must deploy a new virtual appliance and import configurations from the old appliance.
Note

Install a Virtual Appliance
.

/opt/ns/upgrades
partition where the upgrade package is downloaded. You can delete older versions of the appliance from the
upgrades
folder to free up disk space.

.

cz.archive.ubuntu.com

Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 103.0.0.338
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s Virtual Appliance, such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Overview for Virtual Appliance Version 103.0.0.338
The Netskope Virtual Appliance can be used  to steer traffic, as a log parser to discover cloud apps in your environment, or as a Dataplane appliance (DPoP) to act as a proxy server.
Requirements for Virtual Appliance Version 103.0.0.338

Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Netskope appliance releases are numbered in the form of X.X.X where the Xs represent the major, minor, and build release numbers, respectively. For example, appliance release 93.1.0 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 103.0.0.338 goes live. Release numbers are not sequential like 101, 102, and 103. Instead, release numbers jump numerically, like 96.0.0, 99.0.0, and 103.0.0.338, to reflect parity with the Netskope Cloud Releases.
The following table provides the upgrade path to the latest software version.
Note
If you configured the appliance to act as a DPoP appliance and manually deleted the URL database package, you must first disable DPoP before you install the upgrade. Use the following command to disable DPoP:
set dataplane forward-proxy enable false
save
Once you install the upgrade, use the following command to re-enable DPoP:
set dataplane forward-proxy enable true
save

Milestone
Definition
Date
End-of-Life Announcement Date
The date the end-of-sale and end-of-life of a product is announced to the general public.
May 11, 2023
End-of-Life Date
After this date, no urldbz package will be provided to any r99 or earlier release for DPoP appliances. The urldbz package provides the website categorizations service for real-time protection policy match and enforcement for the Netskope Secure Web Gateway (NG SWG).
Nov 15, 2023
End-of-Support Date
The last date to receive applicable service and support for the DPoP r99 and earlier releases. The product becomes obsolete. The old website categorization service will no longer be available for policy enforcement for any appliances running R99 or earlier versions. After this date, all DPoP appliances must upgrade to r103 or newer versions to avoid DP (Data Plane) service degradation.
Jan 14, 2024

EOL for the Secure Forwarder Steering Function
Netskope announces the end-of-life and support for the Secure Forwarder steering function. The Secure Forwarder steering function will not be available on physical and virtual appliances effective October 31, 2023.
Netskope recommends that you migrate to other steering mechanisms that are suitable for your use case as outlined in Netskope’s Traffic Steering documentation. Please contact your Customer Success Manager to discuss your migration plans or for any guidance. We value your feedback and are happy to learn about your migration plan and provide assistance.
For the most current information, refer to:

on our Support site.

## Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 99.0.0
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/new-features-and-enhancements-for-virtual-appliance-version-99-0-0/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:06:56+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:18:04.028023+00:00

Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 99.0.0 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 99.0.0
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s on-premises Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB), such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Overview for Virtual Appliance Version 99.0.0
The Virtual Appliance provides a footprint as part of the CASB and NG-SWG solutions inside an enterprise’s perimeter. The Netskope Virtual Appliance can be used as a Secure Forwarder to steer traffic, as a log parser to discover cloud apps in your environment, or as a Dataplane On-Premises appliance (DPoP) to act as a proxy server.
Requirements for Virtual Appliance Version 99.0.0
Upgrading to version 99.0.0
Before downloading the upgrade package, ensure the following:
Rollback from R99 to R96 or R93.x is supported.
You are running a minimum version R93.x. If you are running appliance versions older than R93.x, or if the root (/) partition is less than 64 GB, you must deploy a new Virtual Appliance and import configurations from the old appliance. To learn more:
Install a Virtual Appliance
.
Note
If your Virtual Appliance uses a 64 GB root (/) partition, then you must ensure that at least 8 GB of free space is available before upgrading.
There is at least 25 GB of free space on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition where the upgrade package is downloaded. You can delete older versions of the appliance from the
upgrades
folder to free up disk space.
To learn more:
Upgrade the Virtual Appliance
.
All the dhcp interfaces on the appliance are configured with a static IP, netmask and gateway.
Export the current appliance configurations to a different host. To learn more:
Exporting Configurations
.
To verify that the host is reachable, run the following telnet command.
nsappliance> telnet host cz.archive.ubuntu.com port 80
Executing telnet as: ['telnet', 'cz.archive.ubuntu.com', '80']
Trying 217.31.202.63...
Connected to mirror-r-01.nic.cz.
Escape character is '^]'.
The following are the
minimum
hardware requirements to install and run the Virtual Appliance.
Component
Requirements
Physical RAM
32 GB
Processor
8-Core
Hard disk space
400 GB is the total disk space required across all partitions. This includes 96 GB for storing and processing logs and 304 GB for the root partitions which store the Netskope software, configuration files, and data files.
You must increase the disk capacity depending on the size of the  logs that are processed daily.
For information on increasing the partition size, see “Increase the Size of the Partition” under Optional Configurations topic on the
Knowledge Portal
.
Note
Netskope recommends that you increase the disk capacity by 5 times the expected daily log collection size.
Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Release number – Netskope appliance releases are designated by the form X.Y.Z where X, Y, and Z are integers. The individual digits represent release major, minor, and build number respectively. It gives 12 months for customers to move to a supported release. For example, appliance release 77 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 99 goes live. Releases that are outside the Netskope support period:
Are not guaranteed to work with the latest cloud releases.
Are no longer tested by Netskope.
Do not receive hotfixes.
Do not receive new feature updates.
At our discretion, we may provide support for releases outside our support period. If a customer encounters an error in a version of software that is other than the latest release, Netskope may require the customer to upgrade to a specified later version to obtain a correction of the error.

This release includes the following new dashboard and existing dashboard changes.

The AI Usage dashboard provides visibility into AI usage in the customer environment on metrics such as:
count of users accessing AI apps
user activities performed
AI related traffic controls

## New Features and Enhancements June 30, 2023
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/new-features-and-enhancements-june-30-2023/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:03:51+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:19:09.604039+00:00

New Features and Enhancements June 30, 2023 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
New Features and Enhancements June 30, 2023
The following enhancements are included in this release:
New Dashboard
The Remote Browser Isolation (RBI) Dashboard is now available in the Netskope Library. This dashboard provides visibility into web traffic isolated by Netskope RBI technology, which helps you monitor your RBI usage and refine your RBI policies & templates applied.
Netskope Library Dashboard Changes
Dashboard changes for the Threat Protection Dashboard include
:
The legend for the widget, “Top 10 IPS Domains” now reads “#Alerts”.
The legend for the widget, “Top IPS Signatures” now reads “#Alerts”.
Private Application Overview Dashboard
Users can now filter by ‘Traffic Type’. This is helpful to distinguish between Netskope Private Access (NPA) and Cloud Firewall (CFW) events.
User Group Filter
When using the attribute ‘User Group’ to filter data, the value lookup is now case insensitive
Known Issue
Insider Threat Dashboard PDF Download Error (269428)
For widgets with a trend line added but no data is available for the time period selected, users may find the error message “Trouble Loading Data”. This will cause the dashboard to fail to download and fail to email a scheduled dashboard.
WORKAROUND
:
Copy the dashboard from the Library to your personal/shared folder.
Edit the dashboard.
Edit Widgets which shows “trouble loading data”.
Navigate to
Edit
>
Y axis
.
Remove the Trend Line.
Save the widget.

New Features and Enhancements May 18, 2023 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
New Features and Enhancements May 18, 2023
The following enhancements are included in this release:
New Dashboard
The User Investigation Dashboard utilizes “User stitching” which ties together multiple user identifiers to provide a complete view of user behavior and data flow. This dashboard shows SaaS identities used by corporate users, the applications being accessed, the instances accessed, the activity performed, and any resulting policy action.
Netskope Library Dashboard Changes
The Insights dashboards on the Overview page now has filters defaulted to ‘Collapsed’ and the default time range is set to ‘Last 7 Days.’ Copy dashboards to a personal/group folder to modify the default time range filter.
The dashboard ‘Cloud Risk Assessment – QBR’, is changed to use ‘Pivot Rank’ for the widget below to accommodate accounts with large datasets.
Top Non Enterprise-Ready Cloud Categories by Uploads
The dashboard ‘Category Summary’, is changed to use ‘Pivot Rank’ for the widgets below to accommodate accounts with large datasets.
Top 10 Applications by Total Bytes
Top 10 Applications by # Users
Top 10 Applications by # Sessions
The dashboard level filter ‘Managed/Sanctioned Apps (Yes/No)’ is modified to a single value filter type for the ‘Cloud Risk Assessment – QBR:’ dashboard.
Netskope Library widgets now have tags; this can be used to help search and filter widgets when building dashboards.

## New Features and Enhancements March 30, 2023
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/new-features-and-enhancements-march-30-2023/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:03:57+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:19:11.845257+00:00

New Features and Enhancements March 30, 2023 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
New Features and Enhancements March 30, 2023
Netskope has planned infrastructure maintenance for multiple management planes starting Thursday, March 30, 2023. During this time, Netskope will make changes to Advanced Analytics. Changes will be visible in your account based on your upgrade date and region.
DLP Incidents Monitoring Dashboard Improvements
Count of object with DLP violations is now aggregated based on the ‘Object_id’ field; this change will provide an object aggregation method consistent with the DLP incidents page on the admin console UI.
Trend of DLP incidents by Creation Date is modified to include count of users, object with DLP incidents.
DLP Incidents – Resolution Time table now includes the ‘Acting User’ and ‘Assignee’ fields.
Shared Library Dashboard Improvements
SaaS Visibility Dashboard – When using the gauge chart type from the widget menu for ‘% of Apps with Poor Trust Score’, it now displays correctly.
Coaching Policy Dashboard – The ‘Justification Reason Information for Blocked users’ widget title name was updated for conciseness.
Unsanctioned IaaS Summary – The text box is resized to show the full sentence at the top of the dashboard.
Threat Protection Dashboard CTEP Language Change to IPS
All occurrences of the word “CTEP” are now changed to “IPS”. In addition, any filters and queries will also reflect the language change.
Application Activity Summary Library – Filter Removal
The “Organization Unit Level1 is not null” filter is no longer available in the Application Activity Summary library > Organization Unit & Application Instance by Total Size of Files widget.
Organizations that do not have org units set up in their environment can get errors for scheduled reports and ad-hoc dashboards when using this filter.
Tip
Remove this filter from your saved dashboards / widgets or you will get an error.
DUNS ID Field Change
The ‘DUNS ID’ field is no longer supported and is removed from Explorer. In addition, this field is removed from widgets and dashboards.
Tip
Remove this field from any saved dashboards / widgets or you will get an error.

## Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 106.0.0.379
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/new-features-and-enhancements-for-virtual-appliance-version-106-0-0-379/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:06:41+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:19:43.449475+00:00

Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 106.0.0.379 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 106.0.0.379
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s Virtual Appliance, such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Overview for Virtual Appliance Version 106.0.0.379
The Netskope Virtual Appliance can be used to steer traffic, as a log parser to discover cloud apps in your environment, or as a Dataplane appliance (DPoP) to act as a proxy server.
Requirements for Virtual Appliance Version 106.0.0.379
Upgrading to version 106.0.0.379
Before downloading the upgrade package, ensure the following:
Rollback from 106.0.0.379 is not supported.
You are running a minimum version of 99.0.0. If you are running appliance versions older than 99.0.0, or if the root (/) partition is less than 64 GB, you must deploy a new Virtual Appliance and import configurations from the old appliance. To learn more:
Install a Virtual Appliance
.
Note
If your Virtual Appliance uses a 64 GB root (/) partition, then you must ensure that at least 8 GB of free space is available before upgrading.
There is at least 25 GB of free space on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition where the upgrade package is downloaded. You can delete older versions of the appliance from the
upgrades
folder to free up disk space.
To learn more:
Upgrade the Virtual Appliance
.
All the dhcp interfaces on the appliance are configured with a static IP, netmask and gateway.
Export the current appliance configurations to a different host. To learn more:
Exporting Configurations
.
To verify that the host is reachable, run the following telnet command.
nsappliance> telnet host cz.archive.ubuntu.com port 80
Executing telnet as: ['telnet', 'cz.archive.ubuntu.com', '80']
Trying 217.31.202.63...
Connected to mirror-r-01.nic.cz.
Escape character is '^]'.
The following are the
minimum
hardware requirements to install and run the Virtual Appliance.
Component
Requirements
Physical RAM
32 GB
Processor
8-Core
Hard disk space
400 GB is the total disk space required across all partitions. This includes 96 GB for storing and processing logs and 304 GB for the root partitions which store the Netskope software, configuration files, and data files.
You must increase the disk capacity depending on the size of the  logs that are processed daily.
For information on increasing the partition size, see “Increase the Size of the Partition” under Optional Configurations topic on the
Knowledge Portal
.
Note
Netskope recommends that you increase the disk capacity by 5 times the expected daily log collection size.
Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Netskope appliance releases are numbered in the form of X.X.X where the Xs represent the major, minor, and build release numbers, respectively. For example, appliance release 96.0.0 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 106.0.0.379 goes live. Release numbers are not sequential like 101, 102, and 103. Instead, release numbers jump numerically, like 99.0.0, 103.0.0.338, and 106.0.0.379, to reflect parity with the Netskope Cloud Releases.
The following table provides the upgrade path to the latest software version.
Note
If you configured the appliance to act as a DPoP appliance and manually deleted the URL database package, you must first disable DPoP before you install the upgrade. Use the following command to disable DPoP:
set dataplane forward-proxy enable false
save
Once you install the upgrade, use the following command to re-enable DPoP:
set dataplane forward-proxy enable true
save
Current version
Upgrade to version
Any version before 99.0.0
99.0.0
99.0.0
106.0.0.379
103.0.0.338
106.0.0.379
Releases that are outside the Netskope support period:
Are not guaranteed to work with the latest cloud releases.
Are no longer tested by Netskope.
Do not receive hotfixes.
Do not receive new feature updates.
At our discretion, we may provide support for releases outside our support period. If a customer encounters an error in a version of software that is other than the latest release, Netskope may require the customer to upgrade to a specified later version to obtain a correction of the error.
For information about end-of-life and end-of-support for appliance releases, refer to
EOL/EOS for DPoP r99
.

On-Premises Appliance Release Notes Version 106.0.0.379
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s on-premises Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB), such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Overview for On-Premises Appliance Version 106.0.0.379
The N2000 and N5000 appliances provide the physical footprint to process and maintain data inside an enterprise’s perimeter.
Note
The N1000, N5000, and N10000 appliances are no longer available for purchase. Netskope continues to support software upgrades on existing N1000, N5000, and N10000 appliances.
The N2000 appliance hardware has been revised and comes preloaded with Appliance software version 106.0.0.379.

Note

To learn more about the appliance:
Overview of Netskope On-Premises Appliance
.
Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Netskope appliance releases are numbered in the form of X.X.X where the Xs represent the major, minor, and build release numbers, respectively. For example, appliance release 96.0.0 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 106.0.0.379 goes live. Release numbers are not sequential like 101, 102, and 103. Instead, release numbers jump numerically, like 99.0.0, 103.0.0.338, and 106.0.0.379, to reflect parity with the Netskope Cloud Releases.
The following table provides the upgrade path to the latest software version.
Current version
Upgrade to version
Any version before 99.0.0
99.0.0
99.0.0
106.0.0.379
103.0.0.338
106.0.0.379
Releases that are outside the Netskope support period:
Are not guaranteed to work with the latest cloud releases.
Are no longer tested by Netskope.
Do not receive hotfixes.
Do not receive new feature updates.
At our discretion, we may provide support for releases outside our support period. If a customer encounters an error in a version of software that is other than the latest release, Netskope may require the customer to upgrade to a specified later version to obtain a correction of the error.
For information about end-of-life and end-of-support for appliance releases, refer to
EOL/EOS for DPoP r99
.
EOL for O365 Auth Proxy On-Premises
Netskope announces the end-of-life and end-of-support date for O365 Auth Proxy On-Premises. Please refer to the table below which describes the milestones, definitions, and dates for the affected product(s):
Milestone
Definition
Date
End-of-Life Announcement Date
The date the end-of-sale and end-of-life of a product is announced to the general public.
Jun 1, 2023
End-of-Life Date
After this date, no new software or bug fixes will be provided.
Jun 30, 2023
End-of-Support Date
The last date to receive applicable service and support for the feature as entitled by active service contracts or by warranty terms and conditions. After this date, all support services for the product are unavailable, and the product becomes obsolete.
Sep 30, 2023
Between now and the end of the support date, Netskope will only support critical bug fixes. Specifically, Netskope will not be providing any new features or enhancements. We encourage customers to migrate O365 Auth Proxy On-Premises deployment to Netskope cloud-based service.
The benefits of moving to Netskope cloud are:
Enjoying the fast and frequent cadence of new features delivered directly in Netskope’s cloud.
Staying up-to-date with the latest and greatest features and security updates.

New Features and Enhancements September 7, 2023
The following are included in this release:
New User Behavior Analytics Dashboard
With this release, the User Behavior Analytics (UBA) dashboard is available in the Netskope Library. Use this dashboard to monitor UBA alerts, refine UBA policies, and reduce investigation time for anomalous user activities.
SaaS Visibility Dashboard
The following dashboards are enhanced to display the top ten results only:
Activity in Non-Corporate Instances
DLP Violations per App Instance
DLP Incidents Status Monitoring
The Average Time to Close (hrs) widget’s unit custom calculation is modified from ‘days’ to ‘hours’ to provide a more precise reading on average resolution time.
The DLP Incidents – Resolution Time widget’s unit custom calculation is modified from ‘days’ to ‘hours’ unit to provide a more precise reading on average resolution time.

## Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 110.0.0
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/new-features-and-enhancements-for-virtual-appliance-version-110-0-0/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:06:34+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:21:00.788584+00:00

Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 110.0.0 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 110.0.0
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s Virtual Appliance, such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Overview for Virtual Appliance Version 110.0.0
The Netskope Virtual Appliance can be used to steer traffic, as a log parser to discover cloud apps in your environment, or as a Dataplane appliance (DPoP) to act as a proxy server.
Requirements for Virtual Appliance Version 110.0.0
Upgrading to version 110.0.0
Before downloading the upgrade package, ensure the following:
Rollback from 110.0.0 is not supported.
You are running a minimum version of 103.0.0.338. If you are running appliance versions older than 103.0.0.338, or if the root (/) partition is less than 64 GB, you must deploy a new Virtual Appliance and import configurations from the old appliance. To learn more:
Install a Virtual Appliance
.
Note
If your Virtual Appliance uses a 64 GB root (/) partition, then you must ensure that at least 8 GB of free space is available before upgrading.
There is at least 25 GB of free space on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition where the upgrade package is downloaded. You can delete older versions of the appliance from the
upgrades
folder to free up disk space.
To learn more:
Upgrade the Virtual Appliance
.
All the dhcp interfaces on the appliance are configured with a static IP, netmask and gateway.
Export the current appliance configurations to a different host. To learn more:
Exporting Configurations
.
To verify that the host is reachable, run the following telnet command.
nsappliance> telnet host cz.archive.ubuntu.com port 80
Executing telnet as: ['telnet', 'cz.archive.ubuntu.com', '80']
Trying 217.31.202.63...
Connected to mirror-r-01.nic.cz.
Escape character is '^]'.
The following are the
minimum
hardware requirements to install and run the Virtual Appliance.
Component
Requirements
Physical RAM
32 GB
Processor
8-Core
Hard disk space
400 GB is the total disk space required across all partitions. This includes 96 GB for storing and processing logs and 304 GB for the root partitions which store the Netskope software, configuration files, and data files.
You must increase the disk capacity depending on the size of the  logs that are processed daily.
For information on increasing the partition size, see “Increase the Size of the Partition” under Optional Configurations topic on the
Knowledge Portal
.
Note
Netskope recommends that you increase the disk capacity by 5 times the expected daily log collection size.
Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Netskope appliance releases are numbered in the form of X.X.X where the Xs represent the major, minor, and build release numbers, respectively. For example, appliance release 99.0.0 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 110.0.0 goes live. Release numbers are not sequential like 101, 102, and 103. Instead, release numbers jump numerically, like 103.0.0.338, 106.0.0.379, and 110.0.0, to reflect parity with the Netskope Cloud Releases.

400 GB is the total disk space required across all partitions. This includes 96 GB for storing and processing logs and 304 GB for the root partitions which store the Netskope software, configuration files, and data files.
You must increase the disk capacity depending on the size of the  logs that are processed daily.
For information on increasing the partition size, see “Increase the Size of the Partition” under Optional Configurations topic on the
Knowledge Portal
.
Note
Netskope recommends that you increase the disk capacity by 5 times the expected daily log collection size.
Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Netskope appliance releases are numbered in the form of X.X.X where the Xs represent the major, minor, and build release numbers, respectively. For example, appliance release 99.0.0 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 110.0.0 goes live. Release numbers are not sequential like 101, 102, and 103. Instead, release numbers jump numerically, like 103.0.0.338, 106.0.0.379, and 110.0.0, to reflect parity with the Netskope Cloud Releases.
The following table provides the upgrade path to the latest software version.
Current version
Upgrade to version
Any version before 103.0.0.338
103.0.0.338
103.0.0.338
110.0.0
106.0.0.379
110.0.0
Releases that are outside the Netskope support period:
Are not guaranteed to work with the latest cloud releases.
Are no longer tested by Netskope.
Do not receive hotfixes.
Do not receive new feature updates.
At our discretion, we may provide support for releases outside our support period. If a customer encounters an error in a version of software that is other than the latest release, Netskope may require the customer to upgrade to a specified later version to obtain a correction of the error.
For information about end-of-life and end-of-support for appliance releases, refer to
EOL/EOS for DPoP r99
.

New Features and Enhancements March 19, 2024 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
New Features and Enhancements March 19, 2024
Advanced Analytics Device Client Data Collection (BETA)
This feature is in Beta. Contact your Netskope Sales team to enable this feature in your account.
We have added a new Advanced Analytics Device Client Data collection and accompanying dashboards. This data collection provides an overview of the most recent organization wide client status.
Client version management ensures your clients are updated with the supported versions, which includes enhancements and future patches.
This data collection provides the following key benefits:
Current Device Status:
What is the current status of devices?
Client Versions in Use
: Which client versions are in use? How many devices are on unsupported, supported, or Golden release versions?
Device Investigation & Troubleshooting
: How many times has a user disabled their client? What is the history of client changes for a given user/device? What are the reasons that a client was disabled?
To learn more:
Device Client Data Collection

Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 113.0.0 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 113.0.0
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s Virtual Appliance, such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Overview for Virtual Appliance Version 113.0.0
The Netskope Virtual Appliance can be used to steer traffic, as a log parser to discover cloud apps in your environment, or as a Dataplane appliance (DPoP) to act as a proxy server.
Requirements for Virtual Appliance Version 113.0.0
Upgrading to version 113.0.0
Before downloading the upgrade package, ensure the following:
You are running a minimum version of 106.0.0.379. If you are running appliance versions older than 106.0.0.379, or if the root (/) partition is less than 64 GB, you must deploy a new Virtual Appliance and import configurations from the old appliance. To learn more:
Install a Virtual Appliance
.
Note
If your Virtual Appliance uses a 64 GB root (/) partition, then you must ensure that at least 8 GB of free space is available before upgrading.
There is at least 25 GB of free space on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition where the upgrade package is downloaded. You can delete older versions of the appliance from the
upgrades
folder to free up disk space.
To learn more:
Upgrade the Virtual Appliance
.
All the dhcp interfaces on the appliance are configured with a static IP, netmask and gateway.
Export the current appliance configurations to a different host. To learn more:
Exporting Configurations
.
To verify that the host is reachable, run the following telnet command.
nsappliance> telnet host cz.archive.ubuntu.com port 80
Executing telnet as: ['telnet', 'cz.archive.ubuntu.com', '80']
Trying 217.31.202.63...
Connected to mirror-r-01.nic.cz.
Escape character is '^]'.

minimum
hardware requirements to install and run the Virtual Appliance.

Physical RAM
32 GB
Processor
8-Core

You must increase the disk capacity depending on the size of the  logs that are processed daily.
For information on increasing the partition size, see “Increase the Size of the Partition” under Optional Configurations topic on the
Knowledge Portal
.
Note

## Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 113.0.0
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/fixed-issues-for-virtual-appliance-version-113-0-0/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:06:28+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:21:55.641765+00:00

Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 113.0.0 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 113.0.0
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s Virtual Appliance, such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Overview for Virtual Appliance Version 113.0.0
The Netskope Virtual Appliance can be used to steer traffic, as a log parser to discover cloud apps in your environment, or as a Dataplane appliance (DPoP) to act as a proxy server.
Requirements for Virtual Appliance Version 113.0.0
Upgrading to version 113.0.0
Before downloading the upgrade package, ensure the following:
You are running a minimum version of 106.0.0.379. If you are running appliance versions older than 106.0.0.379, or if the root (/) partition is less than 64 GB, you must deploy a new Virtual Appliance and import configurations from the old appliance. To learn more:
Install a Virtual Appliance
.
Note
If your Virtual Appliance uses a 64 GB root (/) partition, then you must ensure that at least 8 GB of free space is available before upgrading.
There is at least 25 GB of free space on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition where the upgrade package is downloaded. You can delete older versions of the appliance from the
upgrades
folder to free up disk space.
To learn more:
Upgrade the Virtual Appliance
.
All the dhcp interfaces on the appliance are configured with a static IP, netmask and gateway.
Export the current appliance configurations to a different host. To learn more:
Exporting Configurations
.
To verify that the host is reachable, run the following telnet command.
nsappliance> telnet host cz.archive.ubuntu.com port 80
Executing telnet as: ['telnet', 'cz.archive.ubuntu.com', '80']
Trying 217.31.202.63...
Connected to mirror-r-01.nic.cz.
Escape character is '^]'.
The following are the
minimum
hardware requirements to install and run the Virtual Appliance.
Component
Requirements
Physical RAM
32 GB
Processor
8-Core
Hard disk space
400 GB is the total disk space required across all partitions. This includes 96 GB for storing and processing logs and 304 GB for the root partitions which store the Netskope software, configuration files, and data files.
You must increase the disk capacity depending on the size of the  logs that are processed daily.
For information on increasing the partition size, see “Increase the Size of the Partition” under Optional Configurations topic on the
Knowledge Portal
.
Note
Netskope recommends that you increase the disk capacity by 5 times the expected daily log collection size.
Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Netskope appliance releases are numbered in the form of X.X.X where the Xs represent the major, minor, and build release numbers, respectively. For example, appliance release 103.0.0.338 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 113.0.0 goes live. Release numbers are not sequential like 101, 102, and 103. Instead, release numbers jump numerically, like 106.0.0.379, 110.0.0, and 113.0.0, to reflect parity with the Netskope Cloud Releases.
The following table provides the upgrade path to the latest software version.
Current version
Upgrade to version
Any version before 106.0.0.379
106.0.0.379
106.0.0.379
113.0.0
110.0.0
113.0.0
Releases that are outside the Netskope support period:
Are not guaranteed to work with the latest cloud releases.
Are no longer tested by Netskope.
Do not receive hotfixes.
Do not receive new feature updates.
At our discretion, we may provide support for releases outside our support period. If a customer encounters an error in a version of software that is other than the latest release, Netskope may require the customer to upgrade to a specified later version to obtain a correction of the error.
For information about end-of-life and end-of-support for appliance releases, refer to
EOL/EOS for DPoP r99
.

New Features and Enhancements April 11, 2024
SSPM Evaluation Results Data Collection (GA Controlled)
The “SSPM Evaluation Results” data collection is available in Advanced Analytics as a GA controlled feature; you can now create, schedule, and download reports in the SSPM UI via Netskope Advanced Analytics.

New Features and Enhancements June 27, 2024
SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) Enhancements
The following updated features for SSPM are currently GA-controlled. Contact a member of your Netskope account team to enable these features.
SSPM Dashboard

Findings

Findings
Failed Findings
Passed Findings

Advanced Analytics Fixed Issues

## Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 117.0.0
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/new-features-and-enhancements-for-virtual-appliance-117-0-0/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:06:19+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:23:12.433860+00:00

Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 117.0.0 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 117.0.0
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s Virtual Appliance, such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Requirements for Virtual Appliance Version 117.0.0
Upgrading to version 117.0.0
Before downloading the upgrade package, ensure the following:
You are running a minimum version of 110.0.0. If you are running appliance versions older than 110.0.0, or if the root (/) partition is less than 64 GB, you must deploy a new Virtual Appliance and import configurations from the old appliance. To learn more:
Install a Virtual Appliance
.
Note
If your Virtual Appliance uses a 64 GB root (/) partition, then you must ensure that at least 8 GB of free space is available before upgrading.
There is at least 42 GB of free space on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition where the upgrade package is downloaded. You can delete older versions of the appliance from the
upgrades
folder to free up disk space.
To learn more:
Upgrade the Virtual Appliance
.
All the dhcp interfaces on the appliance are configured with a static IP, netmask and gateway.
Export the current appliance configurations to a different host. To learn more:
Exporting Configurations
.
To verify that the host is reachable, run the following telnet command.
nsappliance> telnet host cz.archive.ubuntu.com port 80
Executing telnet as: ['telnet', 'cz.archive.ubuntu.com', '80']
Trying 217.31.202.63...
Connected to mirror-r-01.nic.cz.
Escape character is '^]'.
The following are the
minimum
hardware requirements to install and run the Virtual Appliance.
Component
Requirements
Physical RAM
32 GB
Processor
8-Core
Hard disk space
400 GB is the total disk space required across all partitions. This includes 96 GB for storing and processing logs and 304 GB for the root partitions which store the Netskope software, configuration files, and data files.
You must increase the disk capacity depending on the size of the  logs that are processed daily.
For information on increasing the partition size, see “Increase the Size of the Partition” under Optional Configurations topic on the
Knowledge Portal
.
Note
Netskope recommends that you increase the disk capacity by 5 times the expected daily log collection size.
Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Netskope appliance releases are numbered in the form of X.X.X.X where the Xs represent the major, minor, hotfix, and build release numbers, respectively. For example, appliance release 106.0.0.379 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 117.0.0 goes live. Release numbers are not sequential like 101, 102, and 103. Instead, release numbers jump numerically, like 110.0.0, 113.0.0, and 117.0.0, to reflect parity with the Netskope Cloud Releases.
The following table provides the upgrade path to the latest software version.
Current version
Upgrade to version
Any version before 110.0.0
110.0.0
110.0.0
117.0.0
113.0.0
117.0.0
Releases that are outside the Netskope support period:
Are not guaranteed to work with the latest cloud releases.
Are no longer tested by Netskope.
Do not receive hotfixes.
Do not receive new feature updates.
At our discretion, we may provide support for releases outside our support period. If a customer encounters an error in a version of software that is other than the latest release, Netskope may require the customer to upgrade to a specified later version to obtain a correction of the error.

**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:07:37+00:00

On-Premises Appliance Release Notes Version 121.0.0 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
On-Premises Appliance Release Notes Version 121.0.0
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s on-premises Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB), such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Overview for On-Premises Appliance Version 121.0.0
The N2000 and N5000 appliances provide the physical footprint to process and maintain data inside an enterprise’s perimeter.
Note
The N1000, N5000, and N10000 appliances are no longer available for purchase. Netskope continues to support software upgrades on existing N1000, N5000, and N10000 appliances.
The N2000 appliance hardware has been revised and comes preloaded with Appliance software version 121.0.0.
The following are the specifications of the new appliance hardware.
Interface
Ports
Speed
IPMI
1g
eth0
Management
1g
eth1
Aux1
1g
eth2
Tap
1g
eth3

eth4

10g

In (Inbound)
10g
The following are the specifications of the old appliance hardware.
N2000
N5000 Series II
CPU
Dual 16 core
Dual 10 core
Memory
512 GB DDR4
768 GB DDR4

4x 1.2 TB Intel SSD
12x 1.2 TB SSD
I/O
(2x 10gbe), 1x gbe ipmi, 1x gbe mgmt, 3x gbe
(2x 10gbe) 1x gbe ipmi, 1x gbe mgmt, 3x gbe
Power
Dual redundant 800W
Dual redundant 750W
Note
To move to version 121.0.0, you must be running a minimum version 113.0.0 since Netskope supports upgrades up to two versions prior to the current version.
To learn more about the appliance:
Overview of Netskope On-Premises Appliance
.
Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Netskope appliance releases are numbered in the form of X.X.X.X where the Xs represent the major, minor, hotfix, and build release numbers, respectively. For example, appliance release 110.0.0 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 121.0.0 goes live. Release numbers are not sequential like 101, 102, and 103. Instead, release numbers jump numerically, like 113.0.0, 117.0.0, and 121.0.0, to reflect parity with the Netskope Cloud Releases.
The following table provides the upgrade path to the latest software version.
Current version
Upgrade to version
Any version before 113.0.0
113.0.0
113.0.0
121.0.0
117.0.0
121.0.0
Releases that are outside the Netskope support period:
Are not guaranteed to work with the latest cloud releases.
Are no longer tested by Netskope.
Do not receive hotfixes.
Do not receive new feature updates.
At our discretion, we may provide support for releases outside our support period. If a customer encounters an error in a version of software that is other than the latest release, Netskope may require the customer to upgrade to a specified later version to obtain a correction of the error.
Netskope MIB File
The following is the Netskope MIB file for 121.0.0:
NETSKOPE-APPLIANCE-MIB-APL121

Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 121.0.0 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 121.0.0
Release Date: December 9, 2024
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s Virtual Appliance, such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Requirements for Virtual Appliance Version 121.0.0
Upgrading to version 121.0.0
Before downloading the upgrade package, ensure the following:
You are running a minimum version of 113.0.0. If you are running appliance versions older than 113.0.0, or if the root (/) partition is less than 64 GB, you must deploy a new Virtual Appliance and import configurations from the old appliance. To learn more:
Install a Virtual Appliance
.
Note
If your Virtual Appliance uses a 64 GB root (/) partition, then you must ensure that at least 8 GB of free space is available before upgrading.
There is at least 42 GB of free space on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition where the upgrade package is downloaded. You can delete older versions of the appliance from the
upgrades
folder to free up disk space.
To learn more:
Upgrade the Virtual Appliance
.
All the dhcp interfaces on the appliance are configured with a static IP, netmask and gateway.
Export the current appliance configurations to a different host. To learn more:
Exporting Configurations
.
To verify that the host is reachable, run the following telnet command.
nsappliance> telnet host cz.archive.ubuntu.com port 80
Executing telnet as: ['telnet', 'cz.archive.ubuntu.com', '80']
Trying 217.31.202.63...
Connected to mirror-r-01.nic.cz.
Escape character is '^]'.
The following are the
minimum
hardware requirements to install and run the Virtual Appliance.
Component
Requirements
Physical RAM
32 GB
Processor
8-Core
Hard disk space
400 GB is the total disk space required across all partitions. This includes 96 GB for storing and processing logs and 304 GB for the root partitions which store the Netskope software, configuration files, and data files.
You must increase the disk capacity depending on the size of the  logs that are processed daily.
For information on increasing the partition size, see “Increase the Size of the Partition” under Optional Configurations topic on the
Knowledge Portal
.
Note
Netskope recommends that you increase the disk capacity by 5 times the expected daily log collection size.

## New Features and Enhancements December 12, 2024
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/new-features-and-enhancements-december-12-2024/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:03:41+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:24:36.313846+00:00

New Features and Enhancements December 12, 2024 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
New Features and Enhancements December 12, 2024
The new features and enhancements are available for the following MPs:
KSA (SA-RUH1)
SIN (SG-SIN2)
UK (UK-LON3)
ZUR (CH-ZUR2)
AU (AU-MEL2)
EU (DE-FRA2, DE-FR4, NL-AM2)
The new features and enhancements are forthcoming for U.S. MPs.
Custom Filter Enhancements
Data Explorer field search based on field label, description, or field group is now available.
Separated options to add text boxes and markdown text boxes to a dashboard.
Added support for an expanded view for widgets on a dashboard.
Added
Custom expression
and
New group
filter options to Data Explorer. You can now
AND
and
OR
logic between filter groups.
Added an expanded view option for dashboard tiles. Select
View
>
Expanded
from a dashboard tile to see a detailed view of the tile.
SaaS Security Posture Dashboard
Added a ‘Policy’ filter for the ‘SaaS Security Posture Dashboard’ to allow users to filter dashboard results based on policies created from custom or predefined rules.
Admins can leverage these results to access and analyze the posture of their SaaS and IaaS resources with industry benchmarks and best practices.
To learn more:
Security Posture Policy
Netskope Library Dashboards
Dashboards in the Netskope Library with ‘Map (legacy)’ type widgets are updated to use ‘Google Maps’ visualization type. Any copies of these dashboards or widgets using ‘Map (legacy)’ visualization in a personal or group folder have been automatically converted as well.
Cloud Risk Assessment – QBR
Alerts by User Location
Data Governance & Privacy Dashboard
Destination Countries with Critical & High DLP Alerts
Private Application Overview
Netskope Data Centers
CISO Dashboard
Alerts by Location
Users by Location
CISO Dashboard – No period Comparison
Alerts by Location
Users by Location
CISO Dashboard with Top OUs
Alerts by Location
Users by Location
Cloud Risk Assessment
Users by Location
Alerts by Location
New Visualizations
Users by Location
There may be some visual discrepancies with the data point size of your personal copies of the dashboards and widgets, as ‘Map(Legacy)’ and Google Maps use different configurations. Best practice is to save a copy from the Netskope Library to your Personal folder and update or edit the widgets using the following options:
From top right-hand side of dashboard select ‘Edit’ from the dropdown menu; select ‘Edit’ again from three-dot menu from the widget.
From the ‘Plot’ tab of the chart edit menu, select ‘Points’.
For finer adjustments to data point size, switch to the ‘Points’ tab, adjust the data point size by setting Radius Units to Pixels, then adjust ‘Minimum Radius’ and ‘Maximum Radius’ to meet your needs.

CCI Gen AI Attributes
New CCI attributes are available for the Application Events, Page Events, Alerts, and Incidents data collection. Use these attributes in dashboards to provide visibility and better understanding of AI integrated applications in your environment. The following table lists the field names and descriptions.
FIELD NAME
FIELD DESCRIPTION
Uses GenAI
Does the app use Gen AI?
Disable GenAI
Does the app allow disabling Gen AI?
Customer data for learning
Does the app use customer data for training AI models?
Data sharing with GenAI vendor
Does the app share the data with third-party Gen AI vendor?
Tenant isolation or private instances for GenAI
Does the app support tenant isolation or private instance for Gen AI?
AI risk regulations and compliance
Adoption of regulatory & compliance standards
GenAI usage policy
Is there a documented Gen AI policy?
Security assessment of GenAI vendor
Does the vulnerability assessment include checks for OWASP top 10 vulnerabilities for LLMs?

## Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 124.0.0.125
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/fixed-issues-for-virtual-appliance-version-124-0-0-125/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:06:09+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:26:20.661055+00:00

Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 124.0.0.125 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 124.0.0.125
Release Date: May 27, 2025
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s Virtual Appliance, such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Requirements for Virtual Appliance Version 124.0.0.125
Upgrading to Version 124.0.0.125
Before downloading the upgrade package, ensure the following:
You are running a minimum version of 117.0.0. If you are running appliance versions older than 117.0.0, or if the root (/) partition is less than or equal to 64 GB, you must deploy a new Virtual Appliance and import configurations from the old appliance. To learn more:
Install a Virtual Appliance
.
There is at least 42 GB of free space on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition where the upgrade package is downloaded. You can delete older versions of the appliance from the
upgrades
folder to free up disk space.
To learn more:
Upgrade the Virtual Appliance
.
All the dhcp interfaces on the appliance are configured with a static IP, netmask and gateway.
Export the current appliance configurations to a different host. To learn more:
Exporting Configurations
.
To verify that the host is reachable, run the following telnet command.
nsappliance> telnet host cz.archive.ubuntu.com port 80
Executing telnet as: ['telnet', 'cz.archive.ubuntu.com', '80']
Trying 217.31.202.63...
Connected to mirror-r-01.nic.cz.
Escape character is '^]'.
Important
Due to space limitations on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition, you must complete the following steps to upgrade to Appliance software version 124.0.0.125.
To upgrade to Appliance software version 124.0.0.125:
Log in to nsshell.
Use the following command to download the appliance software AUP package:
upgrade download software version 124.0.0.125
You must delete all other packages. For DPoP, you must delete the urldb, threat-feed, and software packages. For OPLP, you must delete the threat-feed and software packages.
Use the following commands to see all listed versions of the packages:
upgrade urldb list
upgrade threat-feed list
upgrade software list
Use the following commands to delete all listed versions:
Note
Do not delete the 124.0.0.125 software package.
For all package types, you must delete the locally available packages. You cannot delete the remotely available packages.
upgrade urldb delete version $version
upgrade threat-feed delete version $version
upgrade software delete version $version
To prepare the software package, run the following commands:
upgrade software prepare version 124.0.0.125
upgrade software status prepare
If you are unable to prepare the software package, you must contact Netskope Support.
For DPoP, you must download the urldb package before installing Appliance version 124.0.0.125. Use the
upgrade urldb list
command, then download the latest version with the
upgrade urldb download $Version
command.
Use the following command to upgrade to Appliance version 124.0.0.125:
upgrade software install version 124.0.0.125
The following are the
minimum
hardware requirements to install and run the Virtual Appliance.
Component
Requirements
Physical RAM
32 GB
Processor
8-Core
Hard disk space
400 GB is the total disk space required across all partitions. This includes 96 GB for storing and processing logs and 304 GB for the root partitions which store the Netskope software, configuration files, and data files.
You must increase the disk capacity depending on the size of the  logs that are processed daily.
For information on increasing the partition size, see “Increase the Size of the Partition” under Optional Configurations topic on the
Knowledge Portal
.
Note
Netskope recommends that you increase the disk capacity by 5 times the expected daily log collection size.
Rolling Back Version 124.0.0.125
To roll back Appliance software version 124.0.0.125:
Log in to nsshell and use the following command:
rollback software-image
Note that the status for
mongodb
will be
FATAL
.
Exit nsshell and select bash using a one-time token.
Run the following commands:
lcgo lcmongo-infrastructure
nsadmin@lcmongo-infrastructure:~$ sudo rm -rf /var/lib/mongodb/*
nsadmin@lcmongo-infrastructure:~$ sudo supervisorctl restart mongodb
mongodb: ERROR (not running)
mongodb: started
Log in to nsshell again. All services should be
RUNNING
except for
mongoinit
.
Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Netskope appliance releases are numbered in the form of X.X.X.X where the Xs represent the major, minor, hotfix, and build release numbers, respectively. For example, appliance release 113.0.0 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 124.0.0.125 goes live. Release numbers are not sequential like 101, 102, and 103. Instead, release numbers jump numerically, like 117.0.0, 121.0.0, and 124.0.0.125, to reflect parity with the Netskope Cloud Releases.
The following table provides the upgrade path to the latest software version.
Current version
Upgrade to version
Any version before 117.0.0
117.0.0
117.0.0
124.0.0.125
121.0.0
124.0.0.125
Releases that are outside the Netskope support period:
Are not guaranteed to work with the latest cloud releases.
Are no longer tested by Netskope.
Do not receive hotfixes.
Do not receive new feature updates.
At our discretion, we may provide support for releases outside our support period. If a customer encounters an error in a version of software that is other than the latest release, Netskope may require the customer to upgrade to a specified later version to obtain a correction of the error.
Hash Values for Virtual Appliance Installation Files
The following table provides the md5sum and sha256sum values for the Virtual Appliance installer files on VMware ESX, Microsoft Hyper-V, and Linux KVM platforms for version 124.0.0.125.
File Type
md5sum
sha256sum
ESX OVA
ff4d3c96c1cfbee011dbe860c43f0025
a10363c549beff758a4e17aae16f12aa3b6f1c033eeba13c7aa67f1dc8611877
Hyper-V Image
85e77ad9955df58ecfb8190d908fbcff
0d251976c73ba60554b98cce14d587341d4b9a3bd3de8cf995535f03fdf1c8a3
KVM Image
1b63c72e4294c7c66876b4a6409de8de
40a54b018cc8319e3a6918747615a5f70bd859398cd2d01467b262d10cfba1d0

The following is the Netskope MIB file for 124.0.0.125:

Inline App Connector Release AC-127.0.0 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Inline App Connector Release AC-127.0.0
Published on: June 10, 2025
We are excited to announce our release updates! Get the latest features, issues fixed, and other updates in this release.
The Netskope Cloud release includes API Data Protection, Behavior Analytics, CASB Inline Protection, CCI, CFW, CT, Data Lineage, DLP, DNSaaS, EB, Forensics, Log Streaming, NAA, Chrome Extension, NG SWG, NPA,RBAC, RBI, Reports, REST API, Skope IT, SSPM, Steering, Threat Protection, Transaction Events, User Provisioning and Authentication.
Deployments occur over a one-week window. If you do not see this feature in your tenant immediately, please wait until the deployment period has concluded.
To check your tenant software version, navigate to
Settings > General
.
The Inline App Connector release AC-127.0.0 includes the following releases:
AC-125.0.5
AC-126.1.0
AC-126.2.0
AC-127.0.0

## New Features and Enhancements July 3, 2025

New Features and Enhancements July 3, 2025 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
New Features and Enhancements July 3, 2025
Device Client Overview Dashboard – Device Version Table Enhancement
Conditional color coding is enabled for the attribute ’Client Supported Status’. This is reflected in the ‘Device Overview Dashboard’ from the Netskope Library, as well as any custom dashboard users create using this field.
‘Supported’ versions are referring to client versions that are still downloadable from Netskope, and vice versa.
Broken Widgets Fixed Issue
Fixed the error for
Incident
>
Object
>
Object Name
when the account is not enabled for RBAC and the
Tenant Privacy Field
>
Object
is enabled. This resulted in widgets not displaying correctly.

## Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 128.0.0
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/new-features-and-enhancements-for-virtual-appliance-version-128-0-0/
**Last Modified:** 2025-08-31T02:05:56+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:27:18.791963+00:00

Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 128.0.0 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 128.0.0
Release Date: August 5, 2025
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s Virtual Appliance, such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Requirements for Virtual Appliance Version 128.0.0
Upgrading to version 128.0.0
Before downloading the upgrade package, ensure the following:
You are running a minimum version of 121.0.0. If you are running appliance versions older than 121.0.0, or if the root (/) partition is less than 64 GB, you must deploy a new Virtual Appliance and import configurations from the old appliance. To learn more:
Install a Virtual Appliance
.
Note
If your Virtual Appliance uses a 64 GB root (/) partition, then you must ensure that at least 8 GB of free space is available before upgrading.
There is at least 42 GB of free space on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition where the upgrade package is downloaded. You can delete older versions of the appliance from the
upgrades
folder to free up disk space.
To learn more:
Upgrade the Virtual Appliance
.
All the dhcp interfaces on the appliance are configured with a static IP, netmask and gateway.
Export the current appliance configurations to a different host. To learn more:
Exporting Configurations
.
To verify that the host is reachable, run the following telnet command.
nsappliance> telnet host cz.archive.ubuntu.com port 80
Executing telnet as: ['telnet', 'cz.archive.ubuntu.com', '80']
Trying 217.31.202.63...
Connected to mirror-r-01.nic.cz.
Escape character is '^]'.
Important
Due to space limitations on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition, when upgrading to Appliance software version 128.0.0 directly from version 121.0.0, you must complete the following steps.
To upgrade to Appliance software version 128.0.0 directly from version 121.0.0:
Log in to nsshell.
Use the following command to download the appliance software AUP package:
upgrade download software version 128.0.0.153
You must delete all other packages. For DPoP, you must delete the urldb, threat-feed, and software packages. For OPLP, you must delete the threat-feed and software packages.
Use the following commands to see all listed versions of the packages:
upgrade urldb list
upgrade threat-feed list
upgrade software list
Use the following commands to delete all listed versions:
Note
Do not delete the 128.0.0.153 software package.
For all package types, you must delete the locally available packages. You cannot delete the remotely available packages.
upgrade urldb delete version $version
upgrade threat-feed delete version $version
upgrade software delete version $version
To prepare the software package, run the following commands:
upgrade software prepare version 128.0.0.153
upgrade software status prepare
If you are unable to prepare the software package, you must contact Netskope Support.
For DPoP, you must download the urldb package before installing Appliance version 128.0.0.153. Use the
upgrade urldb list
command, then download the latest version with the
upgrade urldb download $Version
command.
Use the following command to upgrade to Appliance version 128.0.0.153:
upgrade software install version 128.0.0.153
The following are the
minimum
hardware requirements to install and run the Virtual Appliance.
Component
Requirements
Physical RAM
32 GB
Processor
8-Core
Hard disk space
400 GB is the total disk space required across all partitions. This includes 96 GB for storing and processing logs and 304 GB for the root partitions which store the Netskope software, configuration files, and data files.
You must increase the disk capacity depending on the size of the  logs that are processed daily.
For information on increasing the partition size, see “Increase the Size of the Partition” under Optional Configurations topic on the
Knowledge Portal
.
Note
Netskope recommends that you increase the disk capacity by 5 times the expected daily log collection size.
Rolling Back Version 128.0.0.153
To roll back Appliance software version 128.0.0.153:
Log in to nsshell and use the following command:
rollback software-image
Note that the status for
mongodb
will be
FATAL
.
Exit nsshell and select bash using a one-time token.
Run the following commands:
lcgo lcmongo-infrastructure
nsadmin@lcmongo-infrastructure:~$ sudo rm -rf /var/lib/mongodb/*
nsadmin@lcmongo-infrastructure:~$ sudo supervisorctl restart mongodb
mongodb: ERROR (not running)
mongodb: started
Log in to nsshell again. All services should be
RUNNING
except for
mongoinit
.
Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Netskope appliance releases are numbered in the form of X.X.X.X where the Xs represent the major, minor, hotfix, and build release numbers, respectively. For example, appliance release 110.0.0 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 128.0.0 goes live. Release numbers are not sequential like 101, 102, and 103. Instead, release numbers jump numerically, like 121.0.0, 124.0.0.125, and 128.0.0, to reflect parity with the Netskope Cloud Releases.
The following table provides the upgrade path to the latest software version.
Current version
Upgrade to version
Any version before 121.0.0
121.0.0
121.0.0
128.0.0
124.0.0.125
128.0.0
Releases that are outside the Netskope support period:
Are not guaranteed to work with the latest cloud releases.
Are no longer tested by Netskope.
Do not receive hotfixes.
Do not receive new feature updates.
At our discretion, we may provide support for releases outside our support period. If a customer encounters an error in a version of software that is other than the latest release, Netskope may require the customer to upgrade to a specified later version to obtain a correction of the error.
Hash Values for Virtual Appliance Installation Files
The following table provides the md5sum and sha256sum values for the Virtual Appliance installer files on VMware ESX, Microsoft Hyper-V, and Linux KVM platforms for version 128.0.0.
File Type
md5sum
sha256sum
ESX OVA
dac5963ca400c60669daf3f0d8f22b77
dfa6531009461c96fe80235093316471d69927b2371363acd159f4d79aaafb8d
Hyper-V Image
eaf6ee0817205ec13fbb44392c8e2702
c3853e54d649befd80a311d07547729a03b132a5d62b22c89ab70e65883d63fd
KVM Image
0bd29239c0513a8cee63facc14280fc0
40354eca330e6eee44b23e2f7463ef524c7755bdfb191661bf2d7f8d9d27421e

NETSKOPE-APPLIANCE-MIB-128.0.0

## New Features and Enhancements September 5, 2025
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/new-features-and-enhancements-september-5-2025/
**Last Modified:** 2025-09-08T14:05:29+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:27:56.567565+00:00

New Features and Enhancements September 5, 2025 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
New Features and Enhancements September 5, 2025
New Application Category Dashboard
The ‘Application Category Dashboard’ is a new Netskope Library addition. This dashboard provides detailed visibility into the application categories detected in your environment, including:
Top used applications, both managed and unmanaged, in each category
Risky applications, traffic, and data movement in each category
Policies & alerts triggered by applications in each category
Use this dashboard to:
Identify top used applications in each category to reduce application redundancy
Better understand and control the usage of unmanaged & risky applications in each category
Monitor sensitive/risky traffic & data movement in each category
For further customization, save a copy to your personal or Group folder. This report is available through the Reports (New Experience) portal.
To learn more:
Dashboards Overview

## New Features and Enhancements November 14, 2025
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/new-features-and-enhancements-november-14-2025/
**Last Modified:** 2025-12-12T23:23:31+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:28:49.376461+00:00

New Features and Enhancements November 14, 2025 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
New Features and Enhancements November 14, 2025
AI Usage Dashboard
The following enhancements are included with this release:
The Dashboard filter
Category
previously used the
Other Category
field as the underlying filtering field, but now uses the
Category
field instead.
The Dashboard filter
Category
will no longer apply to the widget
Top 20 User Groups with High AI Usage
, this widget now conforms to widget-level custom filters.
These change are currently rolled out for customers on MEL2 MP, and will be applied for all other regions on Dec 5th and will be applied to all users.
Transaction Events
The
Pause/Resume Transaction Events
feature is suspended for customers on MEL2 MP. Tenants with transaction events enabled based on entitlements will continue to ingest events even if the
Pause
button from the UI tooltip is clicked. Dashboards and data explorer will continue to populate transaction events and users should not be impacted by this change.
For MEL2 tenants only: The UI tooltip for the status of ‘Pause/Resume Transaction Events’ will not accurately display the current status. If ingestion is enabled and users decide to click ‘Pause’, transaction event ingestion will continue even if the tooltip display status shows ‘Paused’. In addition, if ingestion is paused and users click ‘Resume’, transaction event ingestion will NOT continue even if the tooltip display status shows ‘Resumed’.
Private Applications Overview Dashboard from the Shared Library
The following widgets are removed from the dashboard:
Filtered Users
Filtered Applications
Filtered Publishers
Users can view the filtered in the dashboard level filters instead. These changes are applied to MEL2 MP tenants.

AI Usage Dashboard
The following enhancements are included with this release:

previously used the

The Netskope Cloud release includes API Data Protection, Behavior Analytics, CASB Inline Protection, CCI, CFW, CT, Data Lineage, DLP, DNSaaS, EB, Forensics, Log Streaming, NAA, Chrome Extension, NG SWG, NPA,RBAC, RBI, Reports, REST API, Skope IT, SSPM, Steering, Threat Protection, Transaction Events, User Provisioning and Authentication.
Deployments occur over a one-week window. If you do not see this feature in your tenant immediately, please wait until the deployment period has concluded.

.

New Enterprise Browser Dashboards
With this release, the following two new dashboards are available in the Netskope Library. The Enterprise Browser dashboards provide comprehensive visibility for Netskope Enterprise Browser usage.
Enterprise Browser Usage Monitoring: Understand overall Enterprise Browser usage such as user onboarding, app count, and traffic volume

To learn more:

The Device Events –  Detailed View contains two new fields and a widget on the ‘Device Client Overview’ dashboard to show the client/steering configuration applied on the Netskope clients.
New fields:
Steering Configuration: A set of rules that controls how and what traffic gets steered to Netskope for analysis or bypassed.
Client Configuration: A set of rules and operational parameters that dictate how the Netskope Steering Client behaves.
To learn more:
Device Client Data Collection

## Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 135.0.0
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/new-features-and-enhancements-in-virtual-appliance-135-0-0/
**Last Modified:** 2026-03-31T15:23:05+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:30:43.439774+00:00

Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 135.0.0 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
Virtual Appliance Release Notes Version 135.0.0
Release Date: March 31, 2026
This release provides several improvements for Netskope’s Virtual Appliance, such as new features, enhancements, known issues, and fixed issues.
Requirements for Virtual Appliance Version 135.0.0
Upgrading to version 135.0.0
Before downloading the upgrade package, ensure the following:
You are running a minimum version of 128.0.0. If you are running appliance versions older than 128.0.0, or if the root (/) partition is less than 64 GB, you must deploy a new Virtual Appliance and import configurations from the old appliance. To learn more:
Install a Virtual Appliance
.
Note
If your Virtual Appliance uses a 64 GB root (/) partition, then you must ensure that at least 8 GB of free space is available before upgrading.
There is at least 42 GB of free space on the
/opt/ns/upgrades
partition where the upgrade package is downloaded. You can delete older versions of the appliance from the
upgrades
folder to free up disk space.
To learn more:
Upgrade the Virtual Appliance
.
All the dhcp interfaces on the appliance are configured with a static IP, netmask and gateway.
Export the current appliance configurations to a different host. To learn more:
Exporting Configurations
.
To verify that the host is reachable, run the following telnet command.
nsappliance> telnet host cz.archive.ubuntu.com port 80
Executing telnet as: ['telnet', 'cz.archive.ubuntu.com', '80']
Trying 217.31.202.63...
Connected to mirror-r-01.nic.cz.
Escape character is '^]'.
The following are the
minimum
hardware requirements to install and run the Virtual Appliance.
Component
Requirements
Physical RAM
32 GB
Processor
8-Core
Hard disk space
450 GB is the total disk space required across all partitions. This includes 96 GB for storing and processing logs and 304 GB for the root partitions which store the Netskope software, configuration files, and data files.
You must increase the disk capacity depending on the size of the  logs that are processed daily.
For information on increasing the partition size, see “Increase the Size of the Partition” under Optional Configurations topic on the
Knowledge Portal
.
Note
Netskope recommends that you increase the disk capacity by 5 times the expected daily log collection size.
Appliance Software Version Support
Netskope Appliance software releases are available every 4-months and will have Netskope support up to two previous versions. Direct software upgrades are supported as long as the “from” and “to” software releases are within two versions apart.
Netskope appliance releases are numbered in the form of X.X.X.X where the Xs represent the major, minor, hotfix, and build release numbers, respectively. For example, appliance release 110.0.0 and older releases are deprecated when appliance release 135.0.0 goes live. Release numbers are not sequential like 101, 102, and 103. Instead, release numbers jump numerically, like 128.0.0, 132.0.1 and 135.0.0, to reflect parity with the Netskope Cloud Releases.
The following table provides the upgrade path to the latest software version.
Current version
Upgrade to version
Any version before 128.0.0
128.0.0
128.0.0
135.0.0
132.0.1
135.0.0
Releases that are outside the Netskope support period:
Are not guaranteed to work with the latest cloud releases.
Are no longer tested by Netskope.
Do not receive hotfixes.
Do not receive new feature updates.
At our discretion, we may provide support for releases outside our support period. If a customer encounters an error in a version of software that is other than the latest release, Netskope may require the customer to upgrade to a specified later version to obtain a correction of the error.

## New Features and Enhancements April 17, 2026
**URL:** https://docs.netskope.com/en/new-features-and-enhancements-april-17-2026/
**Last Modified:** 2026-04-18T01:48:27+00:00
**Scraped:** 2026-06-30T10:31:03.502440+00:00

New Features and Enhancements April 17, 2026 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
New Features and Enhancements April 17, 2026
New Dashboard & Data Attributes: AI Security Guardrails
We are pleased to announce the addition of the AI Guardrails
dashboard to the Netskope Advanced Analytics library, along with new data attributes to support custom dashboard creation.
New Library Dashboard
The AI Guardrails dashboard provides out-of-the-box visibility into generative AI activity across your organization. It is designed to help security teams monitor policy enforcement, detect threats, and assess AI risk posture. The dashboard includes:
Total prompts and responses detected across monitored AI applications
Risk category breakdown, including prompt injection & jailbreaking, hate speech, weapons, and keyword matches
Allowed vs. blocked outcome distribution
Top users and applications by detection volume
Threat framework mapping against OWASP Top 10 LLM and MITRE ATLAS
New Data Attributes
To support custom reporting and tailored analysis, the following new fields have been added to the AI Guardrails alert schema in Advanced Analytics:
Attribute
Description
Profile Name
The guardrail profile applied at time of detection
Matched Category Name
The risk category triggered by the interaction
Matched Category Level
Severity level of the matched category
Matched Prompt/Response
The prompt or response that triggered detection
Matched Prompt/Response Level
Severity level of the matched prompt or response
Matched Keyword
Specific keyword(s) that triggered detection
OWASP Top 10 LLM
Mapped OWASP LLM risk classification
MITRE ATLAS
Mapped MITRE ATLAS technique
Matched Content
Full content of the matched interaction
These attributes can be used to build custom widgets and dashboards, apply targeted filters, or enrich existing views with AI-specific threat context.
Getting Started
The AI Guardrails dashboard is available now in the Netskope Advanced Analytics library. New data attributes are populated automatically as part of Alerts data collection, provided AI Guardrails policies are active in your environment.
To learn more:
AI Guardrails Dashboard

New Features and Enhancements April 23, 2026 - Netskope Knowledge Portal
New Features and Enhancements April 23, 2026
New Dashboard: AI Gateway Analytics
Advanced Analytics introduces the AI Gateway Dashboard that gives organizations visibility into traffic to AI agents and AI models (LLMs) through deployed AI Gateways. As enterprises accelerate adoption of large language models (LLMs), this dashboard provides the data teams need to govern AI usage, enforce security policy, optimize token costs, and maintain operational health across all AI providers and models.
The AI Gateway Events data collection is available for users to build and customize their own dashboards. Navigate to Advanced Analytics > Netskope Library to view.
To learn more:
AI Gateway Analytics Dashboard
